skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with complete opacification of a hemithorax to distinguish between massive pleural effusion and total lung collapse/atelectasis.
steps: Assess the position of the trachea and mediastinum relative to the side of the opacification.
If the trachea and mediastinum are displaced away from (contralateral to) the opacity, identify the finding as a space-occupying process like a massive pleural effusion.
If the trachea and mediastinum are shifted toward (ipsilateral to) the opacity, identify the finding as volume loss due to lung collapse or atelectasis.
Use the direction of this shift to rule out incorrect diagnoses that pair the wrong pathology with the observed anatomical displacement.
